mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economy feels the effects of reduced construction activity.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 jobs in a month, it signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 35% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on mechanism where a high level of real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 45% of the periods analyzed, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction-driven mechanism where a simultaneous increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) and a decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) within a month signals an inflationary environment with easing monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real interest rates decline.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase & FEDFUNDS decrease in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A regime-conditional mechanism where a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2% in a month during a period of low inflation (CPIAUCSL growth < 2% annually) signals a healthy labor market without inflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 30% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, the hypothesis is rejected.
